title: handoff
description: Who handed what to whom and how it’s going: one Bot asks another (or a person) to do part of the work, and the result comes back here.

from.description: Who handed it over: usually the producer (Hermes or a Bot, with `bot` set).

to.description: Who took it: one of the person’s Bots (`bot` set: its face and its chat) or a person (initials; no chat link).

title.description: What was handed over, as the line after “Hermes asked Ada”: “to draft the 1.3 release notes”.

context.description: The brief the other side received, quoted as sent: what to do and any limits (“Check with the user before publishing.”).

state.description: sent: handed over, not picked up yet (hourglass). accepted: the other Bot took it. working: it is on it (waving dots and the activity). done: finished, with a result (green check). declined: it said no, with the reason (orange triangle).

activity.description: What the other side is doing now, in the app’s activity words, without its name: “is writing”, “is running the tests”, “is waiting for you”. The client puts the name in front.

done.description: Progress so far, when it can be counted: 2 (of 4 sections).

unit.description: What is counted: sections, files, listings.

summary.description: What came back, one line: “Release notes for 1.3 · 412 words · 3 sections”.

url.description: Where the result is: a gateway file (`hermes-file:`, opened in the Inspector on iPad and Mac, Quick Look on iPhone) or a page.

label.description: The button that opens it: Read the Draft, Open the Report, See the Fix. Defaults to Open.

media.description: A preview when the result is visual: a chart, a mock-up, a photo.

reason.description: Why it was declined, in the other side’s words: “No SSH access to the NAS from this gateway”.

status.description: Where the handoff is. done needs a result; declined needs a reason.

session.description: The gateway session id of the chat where the other Bot does the work. The client draws Open <Bot>’s Chat from it.

chat.description: Where to follow the work. Only for a Bot on the same gateway: the schema requires `to.bot` with it.
